items.hint: the polite offer of food or drink
items.note: Used to politely offer something, often food or drink — "thing は いかがですか" means "Would you like...?" or "How about some...?"

items.scene: accepting something you have just been offered
items.note: A different use of いただきます from the one already learned in Frequently Used Expressions, said before starting a meal — here it means happily accepting something offered, like food or a gift.
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Frequently Used Expressions (matched on target)

items.note: な-adjective — takes な when directly modifying a noun, e.g. きれいな はな (kirei na hana, "pretty flower"); as a predicate it's きれいです.
See the card "What a very old clock!" for とても used with an adjective. Similar to ほんとうに ('really', below) — both intensify an adjective, とても leaning toward 'very' and ほんとうに toward genuine emphasis.
な-adjective — becomes べんりな before a noun.
な-adjective — becomes ゆうめいな before a noun (see "Smith-san went to a famous restaurant yesterday.").

items.note: Irregular negative of いい (ii, good). Regular い-adjectives negate by dropping the final い and adding くない (e.g. たかい → たかくない), but いい becomes よくない instead of the expected いくない.

items.note: See "What kind of place is Nikko?" for どんな used with a noun.
Distinct from ばしょ (basho, 'location') from Lesson 9 — ところ describes what kind of place somewhere is (どんなところですか, 'what kind of place is it?'), while ばしょ asks for a specific spot's whereabouts.
